log.explanation_raw: {"goal": "Make two qubits that are linked so that measuring them always gives the same result (both 0 or both 1).", "steps": [{"n": 1, "action": "Start with both qubits as 0. A single qubit 0 is the column vector |0> = [1, 0] and 1 is |1> = [0, 1]; we write the pair of qubits as |00>.", "state": "|00>"}, {"n": 2, "action": "Apply the Hadamard gate H to the first qubit. It turns |0> into an equal mix (|0> + |1>)/sqrt(2), so the first qubit is now half 0 and half 1, while the second stays 0.", "state": "(|00> + |10>)/sqrt(2)"}, {"n": 3, "action": "Apply CNOT with the first qubit as control and the second as target: flip the second qubit only when the first is 1. |00> stays |00>, and |10> becomes |11>.", "state": "(|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2)"}, {"n": 4, "action": "Measure both qubits. Each part has amplitude 1/sqrt(2), so each outcome has probability (1/sqrt(2))^2 = 0.5.", "state": "(|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2) before measurement; after measurement either |00> or |11>"}], "final_result": "The Bell state (|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2) is created by H on the first qubit followed by CNOT. Measuring gives 00 with probability 0.5 and 11 with probability 0.5; never 01 or 10.", "analogy": "Like two magic coins that are always flipped together: each lands heads or tails at random, but both always show the same side.", "misconception": "Entanglement does not let you send messages faster than light, because each person alone just sees random 0s and 1s.", "uncertain": []}
